grows on ACKs, shrinks on loss (section 6) Connection ID QUIC's name for a connection, independent of addresses (section 12) CUBIC the default congestion control in Linux, Windows and Apple stacks (RFC 9438) Delayed ACK a receiver waiting briefly before acknowledging, up to 40 to 200 ms on Linux (section 7) Ephemeral port the temporary port the client's kernel picks for its end (section 2) FIN, RST orderly close of one direction; abrupt "this connection does not exist" (section 3) Head-of-line blocking bytes that arrived waiting behind a missing earlier byte (section 4) ICMP IP's control messages: errors such as "time exceeded" and "packet too big", and ping (sections 1, 10) MSS maximum segment size: the largest TCP payload per segment, announced in the SYN (section 10) MTU maximum transmission unit: the largest IP packet a link carries (section 10) Nagle's algorithm holding small writes while data is unacknowledged; off with TCP_NODELAY (section 7) NAT network address translation: rewriting private addresses and ports to a public one, with a table of mappings (section 9) Packet, segment, datagram an IP unit; a TCP unit inside it;
